evidence: Dead card navigation silently bounces users to the Dashboard. OutagesScreen.tsx:196 — each outage card's onPress calls `onNavigate?.('OutageDetail', { outageId: outage.id })`; NewsScreen.tsx:137 — each article card calls `onNavigate?.('ArticleDetail', { articleId: article.id })`. But App.tsx renderScreen() is a string switch whose cases run Dashboard/Faults/.../Outages/News/Forms/Buildings/Leases/LeaseDetail/LeaseSignature/More and then `default: return <DashboardScreen onNavigate={handleNavigate} />;` (App.tsx:264-265). There is NO `case 'OutageDetail'` and NO `case 'ArticleDetail'` anywhere (grep for both strings across frontend/apps/mobile/src returns ONLY the two onNavigate call sites — no screen component, no registration). Full traced path: tap outage/news card -> handleNavigate('OutageDetail'|'ArticleDetail', params) sets currentScreen -> switch falls through to default -> renders DashboardScreen. Net user-visible effect: tapping ANY outage card or ANY news article card throws the user back to the Dashboard instead of opening a detail view; the passed outageId/articleId is discarded. Reachable in production (Outages/News are live registered screens; OutagesScreen is wired to the real GET /api/v1/outages API). Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): either add OutageDetailScreen / ArticleDetailScreen components + switch cases (preferred — the detail route is clearly intended), or, as an interim, remove the dead onPress + card Pressable so a non-navigating list doesn't masquerade as tappable. Add an App.tsx navigation test asserting every onNavigate target string used by a screen resolves to a non-default case.

NewsScreen.tsx:91-92 header 'News' / 'Updates from your building and neighbourhood.' and :82-85 filter labels 'All' | 'Building' | 'District' | 'Partners'. PersonMonthsScreen.tsx:78 a hardcoded user-facing validation Alert Alert.alert('Invalid value', 'Enter a whole number between 0 and 20.') plus :93-96 header 'Person-months' / its subtitle, and the inline 'Save' / 'Cancel' / 'Edit' / 'Bulk entry…' button labels (:142,145,155,165). Also OutagesScreen.tsx:209 renders the raw enum via outage.status.replace('_', ' ') ('in progress') with no translation. Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): wrap all of the above in t() and add the missing keys to the 6 locale files, mirroring how the state strings in the same components are already handled.
